organizations.description: United States leadership in Strategic Missions, Electronic Warfare and assured, advanced microelectronics is critical to military dominance and economic sovereignty. Loss of this leadership position threatens U.S. ability to deter adversaries and prevail in conflict. There are additional potential impacts to economic/industrial base equities extending beyond national security. The Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division and the Department of War (DoD) require innovative technological solutions to address current and future security threats in the electromagnetic spectrum (EMS), trusted microelectronics, and strategic missions hardware environments. To engage the broadest set of innovators, NSWC Crane has created the Strategic and Spectrum Missions Advanced Resilient Trusted Systems (S2MARTS) OTA. The S2MARTS OTA (pronounced “SMARTS”) will refine strategies, management planning activities, and implement integrated, complementary solutions that enable broader Department of War (DoD) access to commercial state-of-the-art EMS technologies, advanced microelectronics, radiation-hardened (RAD-HARD) and strategic missions hardware.

We’re committed to helping national investment in research and development come full circle, enabling positive economic impact and ensuring innovative capabilities reach the warfighter. organizations.description: VT-ARC delivers tailored analysis, research, and engineering to address problems of national and global importance. Specializing in forming highly collaborative, trusted partnerships across government, industry, and academia, we enable the critical innovations of tomorrow. VT-ARC performs translational R&D under contract with government and private sector clients. VT-ARC advances innovative and multi-disciplinary applications of hard and soft sciences, technology, and engineering to enhance global competitiveness. The corporation provides multi-disciplinary solutions to complex challenges in Intelligence, Cyber/IT, War/Security, Energy, and Health business sectors. VT-ARC is a private, non-profit corporation affiliated with Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University. As the "Portal to the Power of Virginia Tech" we collaborate closely with Virginia Tech in technical areas as appropriate to leverage the capabilities and expertise of the university.
organizations.label: Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation

organizations.description: The NSAM Center develops advanced manufacturing technologies and deploys them in U.S. industrial facilities to improve manufacturing processes and ultimately reduce the cost and time required to build and repair Navy weapons platforms. The NSAM Center works closely with the Navy’s acquisition community and the War industry to address manufacturing technology issues that negatively impact efficiency, with respect to both cost and cycle time. Projects improve construction and repair processes, such as optimizing production practices, increasing the use of robotic manufacturing methods, investigating modular / packaged units, improving accuracy control, eliminating inefficiencies in Materiel usage, and using advanced manufacturing tools and technologies. The NSAM Center focuses on technologies that improve the affordability of current Navy acquisition programs; new projects will investigate using modern planning systems, automated fabrication technologies, supply chain improvements, streamlined unit / module flow to and within storage and construction areas, wireless data management applications, using 3D models to support production, and developing improved scheduling systems for new, aggressive build strategies.
organizations.label: Naval Shipbuilding and Advanced Manufacturing Center (NSAM)

organizations.description: Develops and deploys innovative metalworking and related manufacturing technologies to reduce the cost and time to build and repair key U.S. Navy ships and weapons platforms, while also collaborating with other relevant manufacturing industries. CNM utilizes a proven approach that blends the virtual center model with in-house technical expertise to ensure that project teams are comprised of the best providers from the industry to identify, develop, select and execute ‘metals-centric’ projects that support ManTech objectives and transition to industry. CNM is managed by Advanced Technology International (ATI) and partners with Edison Welding Institute (EWI), leveraging EWI’s member-based organization that provides applied research, manufacturing support and strategic services. CNM conducts projects that focus on metals and advanced metallic Materiels, metal-based composites, metal manufacturing processes (e.g., additive manufacturing), and joining techniques, coupled with process design control, advanced metrology, and inspection technologies.
organizations.label: Center for Naval Metalworking

organizations.description: Develops improved manufacturing processes for composite-based components and facilitates technology transfer to resolve manufacturing and repair issues identified and prioritized by the Navy’s Program Executive Offices, other DOD services and industry. Operated by Advanced Technology International (ATI) in Summerville, SC, CMTC forms teams of prime contractors, composites industry suppliers and universities to address Navy composites manufacturing technology needs and has strong in-depth knowledge and experience in composites manufacturing technology for all DOD weapon systems. As part of CMTC’s organizational structure, all laboratories, facilities and project labor resources are provided by project teams. This structure results in cost benefit to the Navy, with maximum funding going to project execution. CMTC’s current portfolio includes composites manufacturing projects for four major ship platforms, the F-35 Lightning II aircraft and the CH-53K heavy lift helicopter.
organizations.label: Composites Manufacturing Technology Center

organizations.description: IHEODTD serves as the focal point for EMTC and, as a renowned leader in energetics, provides a full spectrum of capabilities, including energetics research, development, modeling and simulation, engineering, manufacturing technology, production, test and evaluation, and fleet / operations support. EMTC develops solutions to manufacturing problems unique to military system / subsystem acquisition and production requirements and the energetics industry. EMTC does not own or operate any facilities or equipment but is essentially a virtual enterprise that involves government, industry and academia in identifying requirements and executing projects. EMTC identifies weapon system and manufacturing base needs, develops and demonstrates the required manufacturing process technology solutions, and transitions successful results. EMTC understands that energetics are inherently dangerous and require special processes, equipment, facilities, environmental considerations and safety precautions.
organizations.label: Energetics Manufacturing Technology Center

organizations.description: Operated by the Penn State University Applied Research Laboratory in Freeport, PA, EOC is a hybrid between the best components of a university and those of private industry. This relationship enables access to the university’s researchers and scientists, its state-of-the-art facilities and leading-edge research. Application of this hybrid model enables EOC to provide its sponsors with solutions that combine leading-edge research with on-time and on-budget deliveries. EOC and the partner members of its Electro-Optics Alliance (EOA) have completed nearly 40 Navy ManTech projects that have resulted in significant savings to the taxpayer. The EOA advances DoD critical electro-optic manufacturing science and technology, and promotes U.S. preeminence in all areas of electro-optics. Alliance membership is available at no cost to all U.S. companies, government labs and academic institutions involved in electro-optics technology. The EOA is committed to advancing the commercial viability of electro-optics technologies and promoting technology transfer to industry, as well as wide dissemination of new electro-optics-related information.
organizations.label: Electro-Optics Center

organizations.description: iMAST addresses challenges related to Navy and Marine Corps weapon system platforms in the following technical areas: Materiels processing, laser processing, advanced composites, manufacturing systems, repair and sustainment, and complex systems monitoring. iMAST supports the Navy and Marine Corps systems commands, as well as PEOs and Navy laboratories. iMAST also manages the Repair Technology (RepTech) program and applies new and emerging technologies to improve the capabilities of Navy depots, shipyards, Marine Corps Logistics Bases and lower level maintenance activities throughout the fleet. RepTech cooperates and communicates with Navy COEs, the joint depot community, DoD industrial activities, industry, PEOs and university laboratories to improve sustainability, reliability and system availability.
organizations.label: Institute for Manufacturing and Sustainment Technologies

organizations.description: United States Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM) is one of six geographic combatant commands defined by the Department of War's Unified Command Plan (UCP). As a geographic combatant command, USINDOPACOM is in charge of using and integrating United States Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps forces within the USINDOPACOM area of responsibility (AOR) to achieve U.S. national security objectives while protecting national interests. The USINDOPACOM AOR covers more of the globe of any of the other geographic combatant commands and shares borders with all of the other five geographic combatant commands. The commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command reports to the President of the United States through the Secretary of War and is supported by multiple component and sub-unified commands including: U.S. Forces Korea, US Forces Japan, U.S. Special Operations Command Pacific, U.S. Pacific Fleet, U.S. Marine Forces Pacific, U.S. Pacific Air Forces and U.S. Army Pacific. These commands are headquartered in Hawai’i and have forces stationed and deployed throughout the region.
organizations.label: INDOPACOM

organizations.description: The Carderock Division consists of approximately 2,000 scientists, engineers and support personnel working in more than 40 disciplines ranging from fundamental science to applied/in-service engineering. We are the Navy's experts for maritime technology. The Division houses world-class facilities and laboratories. Carderock's Headquarters is located in West Bethesda, Maryland. The Division also conducts research and development at several remote sites across the country. As a major component and field activity of the Naval Sea Systems Command, the Carderock Division provides cradle-to-grave support for its technical products over an enormous range of scientific areas related to surface and undersea platforms. The Division addresses the full spectrum of applied maritime science and technology, from the theoretical and conceptual beginnings, through design and acquisition, to implementation and follow-on engineering. This includes all technical aspects of improving the performance of ships, submarines, military water craft and unmanned vehicles, as well as research for military logistics systems. In addition, the Division is uniquely chartered by Congress to support America's maritime industry.
organizations.label: NSWC Carderock

organizations.description: NSWC Corona Division has served as the Navy's independent assessment agent since 1964. With experience in gauging the Navy's warfighting capability, NSWC Corona is positioned as a leader in NAVSEA data analytics. Utilizing networked data environments, data analytics and visualization, and measurement technology to bridge the Navy's disparate data, Corona enables informed decision-making for the warfighter. The Naval Sea Systems Command field activity provides transparency for warfighting readiness through data analytics and assessment, engineers the fleet’s Live-Virtual-Constructive training environment, and assures the accuracy of measurements as the engineering advisor for the Navy and Marine Corps metrology and calibration programs.
organizations.label: NSWC Corona

organizations.description: NSWC Crane, located in Crane, Indiana is a shore command of the U.S. Navy. NSWC Crane is under the Naval Sea Systems Command headquartered in Washington DC. The mission of NSWC Crane is to provide acquisition engineering, in-service engineering and technical support for sensors, electronics, electronic warfare and special warfare weapons. NSWC Crane also works to apply component and system-level product and industrial engineering to surface sensors, strategic systems, special warfare devices and electronic warfare systems, as well as to execute other responsibilities as assigned by the Commander, Naval Surface Warfare Center.
organizations.label: NSWC Crane

organizations.description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division originally established itself as the major testing area for naval guns and ammunition. Today, it continues to provide the military with the development and integration of warfare systems for the warfighter, warfighting and the future fleet. Our MISSION: We deliver warfare systems to protect our nation and defeat our adversaries. Our VISION: Design, develop, and integrate technologically superior, 21st century warfare systems. The division is headquartered at Dahlgren, VA, and provides Fleet support at the NSWC Dahlgren Division Dam Neck Activity, in Virginia Beach, VA, overlooking the Virginia Capes Fleet Operations Area. NSWCDD conducts advance research in all systems-related areas and pursues scientific disciplines including physics, mathematics, directed energy and digital engineering, modeling and simulation, software, mechanical, electrical and systems engineering, to name a few.
organizations.label: NSWC Dahlgren

organizations.description: Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division is the Department of War Energetics Center and serves as the DoD Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technology Program lead. NSWC IHD focuses on the research, development, test, evaluation and in-service support of energetics and energetic systems as well as works to provide Soldiers, Marines, Sailors, and Airmen worldwide with the information and technological solutions they need to detect/locate, access, identify, render safe, recover/exploit, and dispose of both conventional and unconventional explosive threats. The U.S. Navy, DoD agencies and all allied nations come to NSWC IHD for energetic systems solutions and EOD expertise — we support the warfighter of today and of tomorrow through discoveries that anticipate the future needs for the next generation.
organizations.label: NSWC Indian Head

organizations.description: The mission of NSWC PCD is to conduct research, development, test and evaluation, and in-service support in Mine Warfare, Naval Special Warfare, Diving and Life Support, and Amphibious and Expeditionary Maneuver Warfare Systems, as well as other missions in the Littoral Battlespace.
organizations.label: NSWC Panama City

organizations.description: Provides the Navy's primary technical expertise and facilities for both naval machinery research and development and naval machinery lifecycle engineering. NSWCPD is responsible for the machinery systems core equity of the Ship and Ship Systems Product Area for the United States Navy and serves as a central point for academia and industry to join forces with Navy technical experts to develop solutions to needs in naval machinery. Consistent with its core equity responsibility, NSWCPD fulfills key functions including research, design, development, shipboard and land-based test and evaluation, acquisition support, in-service engineering, Fleet engineering, integrated logistics support and concepts and overall life cycle engineering.
organizations.label: NSWC Philadelphia

organizations.description: Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme Division (NSWC PHD) employs more than 2,500 engineers, scientists, technicians, logisticians, and support personnel who provide the United States Navy surface fleet with integration, test and evaluation, life-cycle engineering, and product support for today’s and tomorrow’s warfare systems. For more than half a century, NSWC PHD has been at the forefront of engineering and product support for the U.S. Navy's combat and weapon systems. From its roots as Naval Ship Missile Systems Engineering Station—servicing and providing overall technical support for Terrier-, Talos-, and Tartar-guided missiles—to its current provision supporting today's and tomorrow's warfare systems, NSWC PHD is the fleet's source for readiness. This page is intended to provide updated information and discussion on NSWC PHD. While this is an open forum, it's also a family friendly one, so please keep your comments and posts clean. In addition to keeping it family friendly, we ask that you follow our posting guidelines here. Comments and posts that do not follow our guidelines will be removed.
organizations.label: NSWC Port Hueneme

organizations.description: Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Keyport (NUWC Keyport) provides technical leadership, engineering expertise, and unique facility complexes that serve to ensure sustainment of undersea warfare superiority for the United States. As one of two divisions of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Keyport’s mission is focused on developing and applying advanced technical capabilities to test, evaluate, field, and maintain undersea warfare systems and related War assets. These advanced technical capabilities directly support the full spectrum of Navy undersea programs. NUWC Keyport is headquartered in the state of Washington on the Puget Sound, about 10 miles west of the city of Seattle and just north of the city of Bremerton. To provide ready support to Fleet operational forces at all major Navy home ports in the Pacific, Keyport also maintains detachments in Southern California and Hawaii, and an operating site in Guam, and an office in Japan. An operating site in Hawthorne, Nevada is used for storage and maintenance of undersea mines. Naval Sea Logistics Center, an echelon five command under Keyport, is located in Pennsylvania and has satellite offices mostly on the East Coast. In addition, Keyport has a presence in Canada in partnership with the Royal Canadian Navy for undersea range operations. Our people frequently travel around the world to support the U.S. Fleet and Allied militaries.
organizations.label: NUWC Keyport

As the world returns to Great Power competition and the recognition that threats against the United States, its allies and interests are both proliferating and becoming more difficult to challenge, the OASW(NCB) is at the forefront of U.S. efforts to sustain and modernize the nuclear deterrent, while simultaneously providing chemical and biological War and compliance with international NCB treaties and agreements. ATI manages Other Transaction Agreement (OTA)-based and Federal Acquisitions Regulations (FAR)-based collaborations, of which many are for the DoD.
organizations.label: Advanced Technology International (ATI)

organizations.label: Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station (TEES)

NSTXL delivers technology to the warfighter by serving as a one-stop-shop to match government requirements with innovative private-sector solutions.
organizations.label: National Security Technology Accelerator (NSTXL)

organizations.label: SOSSEC

organizations.description: Consortium Management Group, Inc. (CMG) manages three Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) consortia – Consortium for Energy, Environment and Demilitarization (CEED); Consortium for Command, Control and Communications in Cyberspace (C5); and Naval Aviation Systems Consortium (NASC), and administers the four OTAs between them. Together, the consortia comprise nearly 2,000 leading companies and academic institutions to provide broad reach, robust competition and a comprehensive range of technologies to meet Government needs. To date, CMG has facilitated more than $2 Billion in project awards on behalf of the Government for its consortia members.
organizations.label: Consortium Management Group (CMG)

organizations.label: National Security Agency Cybersecurity Directorate (CSD)

NJII combines the resources of NJIT with strong industry and government relationships in order to transform ideas into innovative and practical solutions. Through a PIA signed in 2021, NJII promotes War, homeland War/security, and public safety objectives by identifying small business firms, private/public sector agencies, and other educational institutions that may need or can make demonstrably productive use of technology-related assistance from DEVCOM Armaments Center.
organizations.label: New Jersey Innovation Institute (NJII)

Once identified, DEVCOM AC may partner with such manufacturing firms under CRADAs, CTAs, and other T2 activities.
organizations.label: New Jersey Manufacturing Extension Program

organizations.description: The National Security Innovation Council (NSIC) was created to align the Texas War innovation environment with emerging War priorities identified by national security partners. NSIC’s approach includes building an operational model that illustrates national security challenges, identifying Texas-based organizations that can solve the issues, and effectively fostering and guiding the collaboration between the resulting public-private partnership. The DEVCOM Soldier Center executed a PIA with the NSIC, in support of Army Futures Command. The PIA supports the Army Software Factory, a program that leverages a train-with-industry pipeline to empower Soldiers and Army civilians to scope and solve problems with modern software practices. Activities under the PIA may include, among others, coding camps, internships with local industry, and paired programming operations with industry experts. Soldiers and civilians will operate as product teams in roles like product manager, user interface designer, and engineer to help solve existing and future Army problems. The goal of the Software Factory is to bring together concepts of agile methods and high levels of collaboration, to produce products that have direct value to Army users.
organizations.label: National Security Innovation Council (NSIC)

organizations.label: Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office

organizations.description: The Navy Innovation Unit (NIU) is a highly selective Navy Reserve unit operating directly under the Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office. NIU bridges the gap between the speed of commercial technology and the Fleet’s evolving operational needs by recruiting technical and industry experts, connecting them directly with Fleet problems, and deploying agile teams to build and deliver innovative solutions from concept through prototype and deployment.
organizations.label: Navy Innovation Unit
organizations.rawParent: Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office

organizations.description: The Deputy Secretary of War is responsible for the Department's day-to-day business, with primary responsibility for managing the war budget and executing the priorities of the Secretary of War.
organizations.label: Deputy Secretary of War

organizations.description: Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401) is the Department’s lead organization for developing counter-small unmanned aircraft system (C-sUAS) capabilities. Reporting to the Deputy Secretary of War, the jointly manned task force aligns authorities and resources to rapidly deliver joint C-sUAS capabilities, has acquisition and procurement authority, and serves as the supported organization for Department-wide C-sUAS forensics, exploitation, and replication.
organizations.label: Joint Interagency Task Force 401

organizations.description: The Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies (ASW(CT)) advises the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering on critical technologies and leads efforts to develop, transition, and scale technologies that create asymmetric battlefield advantage. ASW(CT) develops strategies and roadmaps and aligns Department investments and transition pathways across six current Critical Technology Areas: Applied AI, Biomanufacturing, Contested Logistics Technologies, Quantum – Battlefield Information Dominance (Q-BID), Scaled Directed Energy, and Scaled Hypersonics.
organizations.label: Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies (ASW(CT))
organizations.rawParent: Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (USW(R&E))

organizations.description: The California Defense Ready Electronics and Microdevices Superhub (CA DREAMS), led by the University of Southern California Information Sciences Institute, accelerates prototyping of radio-frequency microelectronics for 5G/6G and electromagnetic warfare. The hub connects compound-semiconductor laboratories and production-capable fabs with MOSIS 2.0 brokerage, engineering, and workforce resources to speed lab-to-fab transition and reduce prototyping barriers.
organizations.label: California Defense Ready Electronics and Microdevices Superhub (CA DREAMS)

organizations.description: The Commercial Leap Ahead for Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (CLAWS) Hub, led by North Carolina State University, advances domestic wide- and ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor technologies for defense and civilian applications. Through its Research Foundry model, CLAWS accelerates development, prototyping, manufacturing adoption, and workforce growth across power electronics, RF, photonics, sensing, and related applications.
organizations.label: Commercial Leap Ahead for Wide Bandgap Semiconductors Hub (CLAWS)

organizations.description: The Midwest Microelectronics Consortium (MMEC) Hub is a nonprofit, member-led consortium that unites industry, academia, and government to accelerate U.S. microelectronics innovation from lab to fabrication and deployment. MMEC connects members to technology development, infrastructure, workforce, collaboration, and domestic supply-chain resources to strengthen national security and commercial competitiveness.
organizations.label: Midwest Microelectronics Consortium Hub (MMEC)

organizations.description: The Northeast Microelectronics Coalition (NEMC) Hub, a division of the Massachusetts Technology Collaborative, connects companies, academic institutions, FFRDCs, startups, and government partners across the Northeast to accelerate domestic semiconductor prototyping. The hub expands lab-to-fab access, strengthens the regional microelectronics workforce, supports startup maturation, and coordinates shared facilities, expertise, and funding programs.
organizations.label: Northeast Microelectronics Coalition Hub (NEMC)

organizations.description: The Northeast Regional Defense Technology Hub (NORDTECH) connects defense, academic, government, and industry partners to New York and the Northeast's distributed semiconductor infrastructure. Through facilities including the Albany NanoTech Complex and a network of university and industry nanofabrication resources, NORDTECH accelerates microelectronics research, prototyping, workforce development, and transition to domestic production.
organizations.label: Northeast Regional Defense Technology Hub (NORDTECH)
organizations.rawManager: The Research Foundation for The State University of New York

organizations.description: The California-Pacific-Northwest AI Hardware Hub (Northwest-AI-Hub), led from Stanford University, is a network of physical facilities and digital resources that accelerates the lab-to-fab transition of artificial intelligence hardware technologies. The hub connects academic, national laboratory, and industry capabilities across the semiconductor value chain to mature research into scalable manufacturing and system-level demonstrations.
organizations.label: California-Pacific-Northwest AI Hardware Hub (Northwest-AI-Hub)

organizations.description: The Silicon Crossroads Microelectronics Commons (SCMC) Hub, led by the Applied Research Institute, is a Midwest-centered innovation ecosystem that accelerates expansion of the U.S. microelectronics base. The hub connects industry, academia, and government partners to strengthen prototyping, infrastructure, workforce development, collaboration, and the transition of microelectronics technologies from research to domestic production.
organizations.label: Silicon Crossroads Microelectronics Commons Hub (SCMC)

organizations.description: The Southwest Advanced Prototyping (SWAP) Hub, led by Arizona State University, connects semiconductor manufacturers, defense firms, national laboratories, universities, startups, and other partners to deliver flexible and scalable microelectronics prototyping. Hub members use shared fabrication, packaging, testing, and characterization capabilities to accelerate lab-to-fab transition, strengthen domestic supply chains, and develop the microelectronics workforce.
organizations.label: Southwest Advanced Prototyping Hub (SWAP)

organizations.description: Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies (APFIT) provides procurement funding for production-ready technologies that have completed development and are ready to transition into operational use. The program accelerates initial production and fielding, helping bridge the gap between successful prototypes and scaled deployment while prioritizing capabilities with strong warfighter demand.
organizations.label: Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies (APFIT)
organizations.rawParent: Assistant Secretary of War for Mission Capabilities (ASW(MC))

organizations.description: The Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA) is the Department’s enterprise mechanism for translating priority Joint Operational Problems into integrated capability solutions. MEIA brings government, industry, laboratories, and warfighters together early to conduct mission engineering, experiment, integrate, iterate, and prototype solutions, providing decision-makers with technical and operational analysis to accelerate delivery of combat-relevant capabilities.
organizations.label: Mission Engineering and Integration Activity (MEIA)
organizations.rawParent: Assistant Secretary of War for Mission Capabilities (ASW(MC))

organizations.description: The C-UAS Marketplace is the U.S. government's central marketplace for discovering, evaluating, selling, and procuring validated counter-unmanned aircraft systems technologies. Operated by Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401), it provides an entry point for vendors seeking to offer counter-drone capabilities and enables War Department, interagency, and allied users to compare and rapidly acquire vetted systems through streamlined procurement pathways.
organizations.label: Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems Marketplace (C-UAS Marketplace)

organizations.description: The National Guard Bureau Innovation Hub represents NGB J-8/J84I Innovation, the bureau-level gateway for innovation across the National Guard. It brings innovative ideas and solutions from the states to NGB, integrates NGB into the Department’s broader innovation ecosystem, and facilitates relationships and information sharing with industry, academia, and other external partners. The hub also provides entry points for innovation submissions, APFIT opportunities, and industry engagement.
organizations.label: National Guard Bureau Innovation Hub

organizations.description: The Assistant Secretary of War for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (ASW(SO/LIC)) oversees and advocates for Special Operations and Irregular Warfare across the Department, exercises authority, direction, and control over special-operations-peculiar matters relating to the organization, training, and equipping of special operations forces, provides civilian oversight of the SOF enterprise, and advises and supports the Under Secretary of War for Policy on special operations and irregular warfare policy matters.
organizations.label: Assistant Secretary of War for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (ASW(SO/LIC))
organizations.rawParent: Under Secretary of War for Policy (USW(P))

organizations.description: The Secretariat for Special Operations (SSO) is the legally mandated office that assists ASW(SO/LIC) in exercising authority, direction, and control over special-operations-peculiar administration and support of U.S. Special Operations Command, including readiness, organization, resources, equipment, capability development, and civilian personnel. The Secretariat strengthens civilian oversight and integrates special operations governance, resourcing, and capability development.
organizations.label: Secretariat for Special Operations (SSO)
organizations.rawManager: Assistant Secretary of War for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (ASW(SO/LIC))
organizations.rawParent: Assistant Secretary of War for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (ASW(SO/LIC))

organizations.description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) is the Marine Corps portfolio-level ground systems acquisition organization, established in April 2026 to integrate program management and acquisition support across Marine Corps ground capabilities and accelerate delivery of capabilities to Marines. Its Industry Portal provides a direct pathway for industry and innovators to engage on priority capability areas.
organizations.label: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC)

organizations.description: Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity (MCTSSA) provides global technical support for Marine Corps C5ISRT systems and conducts research and development, systems engineering, integration, testing and evaluation, experimentation, prototyping, and software support to inform acquisition decisions and accelerate capabilities to the Fleet Marine Force. In 2024, MCTSSA became the Marine Corps' first Science and Technology Reinvention Laboratory.
organizations.label: Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity (MCTSSA)
organizations.location: Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California

organizations.description: Established October 1, 2009, the Marine Corps Expeditionary Energy Office (E2O) analyzes, develops, and directs Marine Corps operational energy strategy and coordinates the development, experimentation, and transition of energy technologies that increase expeditionary effectiveness, improve energy resilience, and reduce logistics burden.
organizations.label: Marine Corps Expeditionary Energy Office (E2O)

organizations.description: NGA Moonshot Labs is the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency's unclassified innovation hub and collaborative collider space, bringing NGA personnel, mission partners, customers, industry, and academia together to create, experiment, collaborate, and accelerate geospatial-intelligence solutions. Opened in July 2021 at the T-REX innovation center in downtown St. Louis, Moonshot Labs remains featured by NGA as a cross-agency innovation asset.
organizations.label: NGA Moonshot Labs
organizations.location: T-REX Innovation Center, St. Louis, Missouri

organizations.description: The Space Reconnaissance Laboratory (SRL) is the National Reconnaissance Office's federal laboratory for advancing satellite and supporting-infrastructure technologies. SRL connects NRO with academia, industry, other federal laboratories, and nontraditional partners through flexible research agreements, technology-transfer authorities, and recurring technology-scouting mechanisms to accelerate high-impact technologies for space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance.
organizations.label: Space Reconnaissance Laboratory (SRL)

organizations.description: AFRL Southwest is the Air Force Research Laboratory partnership intermediary supported by New Mexico Tech through the Southwest Innovation Alliance (SWIA). It builds partnerships among AFRL, industry, academia, entrepreneurs, and regional stakeholders to accelerate technology transfer and transition, commercialization, collaborative research, and STEM workforce development.
organizations.label: AFRL Southwest
organizations.rawManager: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology

organizations.description: The Air Force Research Laboratory Technology Transition Office serves as AFRL's primary system integrator, connecting the laboratory, mission partners and industry directly to the acquisition community to accelerate technology system delivery. It integrates AFWERX, SpaceWERX and components of former AFRL capability and partnering organizations.
organizations.label: Air Force Research Laboratory Technology Transition Office (TTO)

organizations.description: The Air Force Sustainment Center Software Directorate consolidates software efforts across the Air Force and provides process improvement and engineering expertise for software development, modification, sustainment and engineering services. It oversees the Air Force Sustainment Center's major software engineering organizations.
organizations.label: Air Force Sustainment Center Software Directorate (AFSC/SW)

organizations.description: Kessel Run is an Air Force software organization delivering operational command-and-control capabilities through user-centered, iterative software development. Based at Hanscom AFB, it operates within the DAF PAE C3BM portfolio and develops and sustains software supporting air operations and battle management.
organizations.label: Kessel Run
organizations.rawManager: Department of the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Command, Control, Communications and Battle Management (DAF PAE C3BM)
organizations.rawParent: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC)

organizations.description: Project Arc is a selective Air Force innovation program established in July 2020 under AFWERX. It embeds technically skilled Airmen and Guardians with operational organizations to solve mission problems through rapid, cross-disciplinary development, experimentation and transition of locally relevant solutions.
organizations.label: Project Arc

organizations.description: The New Mexico Trade Alliance is an AFRL partnership intermediary supporting AFRL-New Mexico technology transfer, economic and workforce development, small-business engagement and commercialization. Its Air Force PIA began in 2019, and it operates Q Station as a public-facing collaboration and technology engagement hub.
organizations.label: New Mexico Trade Alliance (NMTA)

organizations.description: Pacific Region, operated by the Maui Economic Development Board, is the Air Force Research Laboratory partnership intermediary presence in Hawaii. It connects Air Force technology-transition needs with regional industry, academia and innovation partners across the Pacific through ecosystem engagement, workshops, university collaboration and transition support.
organizations.label: Pacific Region

organizations.description: The University of Massachusetts Lowell Applied Research Corporation is the Partnership Intermediary supporting Hanscom Air Force Base. Its DAF PIA, signed in December 2024, connects government mission organizations with academia, startups, small businesses and industry to accelerate technology transfer, applied research and transition through the Greater Boston innovation ecosystem.
organizations.label: University of Massachusetts Lowell Applied Research Corporation (UMLARC)
organizations.rawParent: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC)

organizations.description: The Space Systems Command Commercial Space Office (COMSO) accelerates commercial partnerships and serves as the primary gateway for the United States Space Force to leverage commercial-space innovation, coordinating commercial engagement and transition efforts across the Space Force, combatant commands, the Department of War, and industry.
organizations.label: Space Systems Command Commercial Space Office (COMSO)

organizations.description: The United States Space Force Front Door is the primary entry point for startups, nontraditional partners, and commercial vendors seeking to engage the Space Force. Launched by Space Systems Command in 2023 and renamed USSF Front Door in September 2025, it operates within COMSO and connects commercial solutions with mission owners and acquisition pathways across the service.
organizations.label: United States Space Force Front Door (USSF Front Door)
organizations.rawParent: Space Systems Command Commercial Space Office (COMSO)

organizations.description: Formerly the Space Domain Awareness Tools, Applications and Processing Lab (SDA TAP Lab), the BMC3I TAP Lab connects commercial innovators with U.S. Space Force mission stakeholders to mature and transition technologies for space domain awareness and battle management, command, control, communications, and space intelligence. Its current focus areas include Battle Damage Indications/Assessment, which improves multisource assessment across the TCPED lifecycle, and Crimson Forge, a secure environment intended to advance commercial capabilities from TRL 4 toward TRL 7/8 and operational programs of record. The lab’s updated engagement pathway includes the Mission Catalyst Summit and phased cohorts with Catalyst Campus.
organizations.label: BMC3I TAP Lab

organizations.description: The Texas Space Commission is the partnership intermediary under a 2026 Air Force Research Laboratory Partnership Intermediary Agreement supporting United States Space Force commercial integration. The agreement accelerates technology scouting and transition from commercial prototypes to operational capabilities while strengthening advanced manufacturing, supply-chain resilience, acquisition pathways, and the national security space industrial base.
organizations.label: Texas Space Commission (TSC)

organizations.description: The U.S. Army Futures and Concepts Command (FCC) is a major subordinate command of Transformation and Training Command responsible for developing and authenticating future concepts, requirements, experimentation, integration, research, and analysis to drive persistent Army modernization.
organizations.label: U.S. Army Futures and Concepts Command (FCC)

organizations.description: Joint Modernization Command plans, prepares, and executes Joint Warfighting Assessments, Project Convergence, and other joint and multinational concept and capability experiments through persistent experimentation, providing objective analysis and recommendations to inform Army continuous transformation.
organizations.label: Joint Modernization Command (JMC)
organizations.rawParent: U.S. Army Futures and Concepts Command (FCC)

organizations.description: The Army Cyber Technology and Innovation Center (ArCTIC) is U.S. Army Cyber Command’s data-centric laboratory focused on innovation and future capabilities, prototyping and assessing cyber, data, and technology solutions to influence operational capability development and transition.
organizations.label: Army Cyber Technology and Innovation Center (ArCTIC)

organizations.description: U.S. Army Communications-Electronics Command (CECOM) is a major subordinate command of Army Materiel Command that integrates and sustains C5ISR and medical materiel readiness for the Army and oversees subordinate centers including the Army Software & Innovation Center.
organizations.label: U.S. Army Communications-Electronics Command (CECOM)

organizations.description: The Army Software & Innovation Center (ASIC) is CECOM's premier organic software center, rapidly delivering full-stack and low-code/no-code software, DevSecOps platforms, electromagnetic-warfare reprogramming, artificial intelligence, and operational readiness support to Army organizations.
organizations.label: Army Software & Innovation Center (ASIC)

organizations.description: The 82nd Airborne Division is the Army's primary airborne division for joint forcible-entry operations and the principal fighting formation of XVIII Airborne Corps, based at Fort Bragg, North Carolina.
organizations.label: 82nd Airborne Division

organizations.description: The Airborne Innovation Lab (AIL) is the 82nd Airborne Division's Soldier-driven innovation hub at Fort Bragg, connecting Paratroopers and partners to rapidly design, prototype, test, and refine tactical solutions using additive manufacturing, robotics, electronics, fabrication, and design-thinking capabilities.
organizations.label: Airborne Innovation Lab (AIL)

organizations.description: The 25th Infantry Division is an Army division based at Schofield Barracks, Hawaii, focused on Indo-Pacific readiness, transformation, experimentation, and combat operations.
organizations.label: 25th Infantry Division

organizations.description: Lightning Labs is the 25th Infantry Division's enduring innovation and experimentation cell, capturing Soldier problems, rapidly prototyping solutions, and refining technologies through field experimentation to improve lethality, survivability, mobility, and operational readiness across the Indo-Pacific.
organizations.label: Lightning Labs

organizations.description: The Maneuver Battle Lab (MBL) conducts combined-arms and cross-domain maneuver experimentation using live prototyping, force-on-force events, modeling, simulation, and analysis to support Soldier and small-unit modernization, future-force concepts, and Army investment decisions.
organizations.label: Maneuver Battle Lab (MBL)

organizations.description: The Maneuver Innovation Lab (MIL) is a Soldier-facing collaborative innovation hub at Fort Benning that connects Soldiers, the Maneuver Battle Lab, DEVCOM, academia, and industry to turn bottom-up operational problems into prototypes and rapidly test potential solutions.
organizations.label: Maneuver Innovation Lab (MIL)

organizations.description: The 10th Mountain Division (Light Infantry) is a globally responsive Army division headquartered at Fort Drum, New York, preparing expeditionary forces for combat while driving tactical adaptation and Soldier-led innovation.
organizations.label: 10th Mountain Division (LI)

organizations.description: The Mountain Innovation Systems Lab is the 10th Mountain Division's Fort Drum innovation capability for rapid experimentation and local production, including additive manufacturing of unmanned-system components and hands-on integration of emerging drone and counter-UAS technologies.
organizations.label: Mountain Innovation Systems Lab

organizations.description: The 1st Cavalry Division is the Army's premier armored division, headquartered at Fort Hood, Texas, and a major operational formation focused on combat readiness, modernization, and transformation.
organizations.label: 1st Cavalry Division

organizations.description: The 1st Cavalry Division Innovation Lab is a Soldier-driven prototyping and experimentation organization at Fort Hood developing tactical technologies, including in-house unmanned aircraft systems and counter-drone solutions, for First Team formations and broader Army transformation efforts.
organizations.label: 1st Cavalry Division Innovation Lab

organizations.description: Project Manager Cyber Warfare (PM CW) was established July 31, 2026 under Capability Program Executive Intelligence and Spectrum Warfare (CPE ISW). It unifies Army offensive and defensive cyber acquisition portfolios and rapidly acquires, prototypes, fields, and sustains integrated cyberspace capabilities using flexible pathways that bring commercial and private-sector technologies to Army cyber forces.
organizations.label: Project Manager Cyber Warfare (PM CW)
organizations.rawManager: Capability Program Executive Intelligence and Spectrum Warfare (CPE ISW)
organizations.rawParent: Assistant Secretary of the Army for Acquisition, Logistics and Technology

organizations.description: The NIWC Atlantic Rapid Capabilities Office accelerates delivery of information warfare and cyber capabilities by using flexible acquisition approaches, commercial solutions openings, rapid prototyping, and direct industry engagement to address urgent operational gaps.
organizations.label: NIWC Atlantic Rapid Capabilities Office (RCO)
organizations.rawParent: Naval Information Warfare Center Atlantic (NIWC Atlantic)

organizations.description: The National Security Plug and Play Consortium (NSPPC), established by the Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office, connects the Navy and Marine Corps with technology companies and nontraditional innovators using other transactions, commercial solutions openings, prize challenges, and other rapid acquisition pathways.
organizations.label: National Security Plug and Play Consortium (NSPPC)
organizations.rawParent: Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office

organizations.description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Robotics & Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS) serves as the Navy's central acquisition node for robotics, autonomous systems, and related artificial intelligence, accelerating the transition of mature commercial and nontraditional technologies and providing an industry Front Door for technology pitches.
organizations.label: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Robotics & Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS)

organizations.description: The Department of the Navy SBIR Experimentation Cell (DON-SEC) connects SBIR/STTR companies and technologies with Navy and Marine Corps experimentation opportunities to generate operational evidence, accelerate transition, and improve the path from prototype to fielded capability.
organizations.label: Department of the Navy SBIR Experimentation Cell (DON-SEC)

organizations.description: FLEETWERX is a Naval Postgraduate School partnership intermediary operated with DEFENSEWERX that connects fleet problems with industry, academia, and nontraditional innovators to accelerate experimentation, prototyping, advanced manufacturing, autonomous logistics, and technology transition.
organizations.label: FLEETWERX

organizations.description: Innovation and Modernization Patuxent River (IMPAX) is NAWCAD's partnership intermediary for rapidly connecting naval aviation problems with small businesses, nontraditional suppliers, academia, and emerging technologies to accelerate prototyping, technology transition, and acquisition.
organizations.label: Innovation and Modernization Patuxent River (IMPAX)
organizations.rawParent: Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD)

organizations.description: NAVY Launch is the Department of the Navy SBIR/STTR commercialization program that helps promising Phase II companies build commercial markets, attract private capital, strengthen business readiness, and transition dual-use technologies into naval acquisition and operational use.
organizations.label: NAVY Launch

organizations.description: The Electronics Manufacturing Center (EMC) is a Navy Manufacturing Technology Center of Excellence operated by Penn State Applied Research Laboratory that develops and transitions advanced electronics manufacturing technologies, processes, and design-to-production capabilities for naval systems and the defense industrial base.
organizations.label: Electronics Manufacturing Center (EMC)

organizations.description: OrthoWorx is a nonprofit orthopedic-industry ecosystem organization in Warsaw, Indiana. As a current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary, it connects Crane with regional industry, workforce, and innovation resources to support technology collaboration and transition.
organizations.label: OrthoWorx, LLC.

organizations.description: Indiana University is a public research university and current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary, supporting research collaboration, technology transfer, talent development, and access to academic expertise for Crane mission areas.
organizations.label: Indiana University

organizations.description: The State of Indiana serves as a current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary, supporting connections among Crane, state economic-development resources, academia, and Indiana's defense and technology industries.
organizations.label: State of Indiana

organizations.description: Radius Indiana is a regional economic-development partnership in southern Indiana and a current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary, connecting Crane with businesses, communities, workforce resources, and technology partners across the region.
organizations.label: Radius Indiana

organizations.description: Ivy Tech Community College Bloomington is a current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary supporting workforce development, technical education, applied learning, and regional industry connections relevant to Crane missions.
organizations.label: Ivy Tech Community College-Bloomington, IN

organizations.description: Purdue University is a public research university and current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary, supporting collaborative research, engineering, technology transition, and workforce development across Crane mission areas.
organizations.label: Purdue University

organizations.description: Purdue Research Foundation supports Purdue's research commercialization, technology transfer, entrepreneurship, and innovation ecosystem and serves as a current NSWC Crane partnership intermediary.
organizations.label: Purdue Research Foundation

organizations.description: The Indiana Research Consortium is a statewide defense-research consortium founded by Indiana University, Purdue University, and the University of Notre Dame to coordinate research across critical defense technology areas. NSWC Crane is a key partner through a multiparty Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA).
organizations.label: Indiana Research Consortium (IRC)

organizations.description: Amplify Bloomington is the current public identity of Dimension Mill, Inc. (The Mill), a regional innovation platform in Bloomington, Indiana. Through its NSWC Crane partnership intermediary relationship and PROPELS accelerator, it supports commercialization of Crane-developed technologies and connects entrepreneurs with defense and regional innovation resources.
organizations.label: Amplify Bloomington (Dimension Mill, Inc.)

organizations.description: Greater New Orleans Development Foundation is a current NIWC Atlantic partnership intermediary that connects small businesses, academic institutions, and emerging-technology developers with Navy and federal laboratory resources to accelerate warfighter capabilities and Gulf Coast defense innovation.
organizations.label: Greater New Orleans Development Foundation, Inc. (GNODF)
organizations.rawParent: Naval Information Warfare Center Atlantic (NIWC Atlantic)

organizations.description: Fairfax City Economic Development is a current NSWC Carderock partnership intermediary supporting the Capital Tech Bridge through technology-transfer, commercialization, reverse-pitch, and industry-engagement activities that connect Navy inventors and mission needs with commercial partners.
organizations.label: Fairfax City Economic Development (FCED)

organizations.description: Pike District Partnership is a nonprofit NSWC Carderock partnership intermediary supporting Capital Tech Bridge industry engagement, small-business access, technology discovery, and collaboration across the Washington-area maritime and defense innovation ecosystem.
organizations.label: Pike District Partnership (PDP)

organizations.description: Polaris Tech Bridge, formerly 401 Tech Bridge, is a current NUWC Newport partnership intermediary and Northeast Tech Bridge partner that connects defense, dual-use, and maritime technology companies with government customers, makerspaces, technology scouting, prototyping, testing, commercialization, and pathways to government contracts.
organizations.label: Polaris Tech Bridge

organizations.description: The University of Rhode Island Research Foundation is a current NUWC Newport partnership intermediary supporting scientific research, technology development, intellectual-property commercialization, industry partnerships, and transition of university and regional innovations into real-world applications. URI Innovations is its current public-facing innovation brand.
organizations.label: University of Rhode Island Research Foundation (URIRF)

organizations.description: SENEDIA, the Alliance for Defense Tech, Talent, and Innovation, is a current NUWC Newport partnership intermediary supporting the Northeast Tech Bridge and connecting government with defense-industry and technology partners to accelerate collaboration and transition of critical undersea, cyber, and defense technologies.
organizations.label: SENEDIA

organizations.description: VelocityTX is a San Antonio bioscience innovation hub and economic-development organization serving as a partnership intermediary for Naval Medical Research Unit San Antonio, part of Navy Medicine Research & Development. The PIA connects military medical researchers with startups, academia, industry, prototype evaluation, joint research, and commercialization pathways.
organizations.label: VelocityTX
organizations.rawParent: Naval Medicine Research and Development Command (NMRDC)

organizations.description: Henry M. Rowan College of Engineering at Rowan University serves as a partnership intermediary for NAWCAD Lakehurst, engaging small businesses, industry, state agencies, and academia to accelerate technology transfer, transition, licensing, and innovation through the Navy's Liberty Tech Bridge ecosystem.
organizations.label: Henry M. Rowan College of Engineering
organizations.rawParent: Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD)

organizations.description: The Naval Postgraduate School Foundation is a non-federal nonprofit partnership intermediary for NPS that connects the school with industry, startups, technology partners, research sponsors, and operational users to accelerate applied research, experimentation, technology commercialization, and solution transition.
organizations.label: Naval Postgraduate School Foundation

organizations.description: Charles County Economic Development Department supports the Western Charles County technology and energetics ecosystem and serves as a partnership intermediary with NSWC Indian Head, helping connect the federal laboratory with local businesses, technology firms, research partners, and commercialization opportunities.
organizations.label: Charles County Economic Development Department (EDD)

organizations.description: University of Mary Washington serves as a partnership intermediary for NSWC Dahlgren and supports the Potomac Tech Bridge by connecting traditional and nontraditional vendors, academia, regional innovators, and Navy mission needs to accelerate collaboration, prototyping, technology transition, and delivery of solutions to the Fleet.
organizations.label: University of Mary Washington (UMW)

organizations.description: U.S. Army Cyber Command is the Army service component command to U.S. Cyber Command and the Army headquarters for cyberspace operations, information advantage, capability development, and rapid cyber innovation. It serves as the parent command for the Army cyber innovation cluster represented in this ecosystem.
organizations.label: U.S. Army Cyber Command (ARCYBER)

organizations.description: FISTA is a Lawton-Fort Sill defense innovation and technology hub that connects Army mission organizations with industry, academia, emerging technology companies, advanced manufacturing, testing, and prototyping resources. Its partnership intermediary relationship supports DEVCOM Armaments Center technology scouting, collaboration, and transition.
organizations.label: Fires Innovation Science and Technology Accelerator Development Trust Authority (FISTA)

organizations.description: University of Dayton Research Institute is a research and engineering organization supporting U.S. Army Cyber Command through a partnership intermediary agreement focused on digital and cyber technology transfer, applied research, commercialization, and transition of defense capabilities.
organizations.label: University of Dayton Research Institute (UDRI)

organizations.description: Metro State Applied Innovation Institute is a 501(c)(3) applied research organization focused on national defense, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies. Its partnership with U.S. Army Cyber Command connects government mission needs with applied research, industry, and nontraditional technology innovators.
organizations.label: Metro State Applied Innovation Institute (MSAII)

organizations.description: RAMP MD is an independent Maryland advanced-manufacturing partnership that connects businesses, government, educational institutions, entrepreneurs, and innovators with additive-manufacturing and prototyping capabilities at Aberdeen Proving Ground. Its Army partnership intermediary role supports DEVCOM Chemical Biological Center technology development and transition.
organizations.label: Regional Advanced Manufacturing Partnership of Maryland (RAMP MD)

organizations.description: Maryland Economic Development Corporation is a public-purpose economic development corporation serving as a partnership intermediary for DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory, supporting business and research partnerships, technology transfer and transition, commercialization, and collaboration with regional innovation ecosystems.
organizations.label: Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO)

organizations.description: The Kyl Institute for National Security is a University of Arizona-affiliated 501(c)(3) nonprofit that replaced and expanded the University of Arizona Applied Research Corporation (UA-ARC) in 2026. It continues the intermediary role connecting national-security research with government, industry, investors, commercialization partners, experimentation, and technology transition.
organizations.label: Kyl Institute for National Security (formerly UA-ARC)

organizations.description: IT-AAC is a nonprofit public-private partnership and standards consortium hosted by the Interoperability Clearinghouse. Working with the Technology Advancement Center under a Department-wide partnership intermediary agreement, it supports DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory and other defense organizations with rapid technology assessment, digital modernization, agile acquisition, and access to commercial innovation.
organizations.label: Information Technology Acquisition Advisory Council (IT-AAC)

organizations.description: DARPAConnect is DARPA’s partnership intermediary program for expanding access to the agency among small businesses, universities, nontraditional performers, and other organizations new to DARPA. Operated through a Partnership Intermediary Agreement with Applied Research Institute, it provides training, outreach, mentoring, proposal-support resources, and regional engagement to help potential performers understand and pursue DARPA opportunities.
organizations.label: DARPAConnect

organizations.description: Technology Transfer, Transition and Commercial Partnerships (T3CP) coordinates Department-wide technology transfer and transition activities, strategic partnerships, intellectual-property commercialization, and pathways that move technologies from the Department’s laboratories to industry and operational use. T3CP supports the DoW laboratory enterprise and national partnership intermediaries including TechLink and MilTech.
organizations.label: Technology Transfer, Transition and Commercial Partnerships (T3CP)
organizations.rawParent: Assistant Secretary of War for Science & Technology (ASW(S&T))

organizations.description: The DIU Bridge Program helps successful commercial technologies overcome barriers between initial Department of War awards and broader adoption. It supports transition by addressing issues such as classified-facility access, security clearances, cyber accreditation, integrated testing, and other scaling obstacles so validated commercial capabilities can reach additional Department customers.
organizations.label: DIU Bridge Program

organizations.description: National Center for Manufacturing Sciences is a nonprofit technology consortium and partnership intermediary supporting U.S. Transportation Command through a Partnership Intermediary Agreement. It connects USTRANSCOM with industry, academia, and nontraditional innovators to identify, evaluate, and transition technologies for transportation and sustainment, including advanced manufacturing, predictive maintenance, automation, and repair.
organizations.label: National Center for Manufacturing Sciences (NCMS)

organizations.description: The Maritime Advanced Technology Accelerator Consortium is an Other Transaction Agreement consortium supporting Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme Division with rapid research, development, prototyping, and production across surface and maritime technology areas including advanced computing, machine learning, directed energy, autonomous and uncrewed systems, and integrated warfare systems. Advanced Technology International serves as consortium manager.
organizations.label: Maritime Advanced Technology Accelerator Consortium (MATAC)

organizations.description: LETHALITY is an Other Transaction Agreement consortium supporting Naval Surface Warfare Center, Corona Division with rapid prototyping across network architecture and infrastructure, cyber, big data analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning, advanced computing, software engineering, virtualization, and other surface and maritime warfighting technologies. Advanced Technology International serves as consortium manager.
organizations.label: Leveraging Enterprise Technologies for Holistic AI, Logistics, Integration, Transformation, and Yield (LETHALITY) Consortium

organizations.description: The DAF TENCAP Consortium is an Other Transaction Agreement consortium focused on rapidly converting emerging Air, Space, Cyber, and Intelligence technologies and prototypes into operational capabilities that improve warfighter lethality, survivability, and combat effectiveness. The United States Air Force awarded the OTA to Advanced Technology International to serve as consortium manager.
organizations.label: Department of the Air Force Tactical Exploitation of National Capabilities (DAF TENCAP) Consortium

organizations.description: The Expeditionary Missions Consortium–Crane supports Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division under an Other Transaction Agreement for basic, applied, and advanced research and prototype projects in expeditionary mission technologies including power and energy, specialized munitions, weapon systems, maneuver and surveillance, integrated software, C3I and cyber, and electro-optic technologies. Advanced Technology International serves as consortium manager.
organizations.label: Expeditionary Missions Consortium–Crane (EMC)

organizations.description: Metals Affordability Initiative III is an Air Force Research Laboratory-sponsored aerospace metals research consortium administered by Advanced Technology International under a cooperative agreement. MAI III pools government and industry resources to develop and accelerate affordable metallic materials, manufacturing processes, qualification methods, and implementation for defense aerospace systems.
organizations.label: Metals Affordability Initiative III (MAI III)

organizations.description: Creative Defense Foundation is a nonprofit national-security innovation organization and the consortium manager for the Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office's National Security Plug and Play Consortium (NSPPC), connecting government mission needs with entrepreneurs, technology companies, and other innovators.
organizations.label: Creative Defense Foundation (CDF)

organizations.description: The Defense Electronics Consortium is an Other Transaction Agreement collaboration focused on strengthening the U.S. defense electronics industrial base. DEC operates under the Cornerstone OTA and connects government with electronics manufacturers, suppliers, academic researchers, and other innovators for prototype projects and technology transition. Advanced Technology International serves as the Consortium Management Firm.
organizations.label: Defense Electronics Consortium (DEC)

organizations.description: The Joint Directed Energy Consortium is the primary Other Transaction agreement vehicle supporting OUSW(R&E) Critical Technologies' Scaled Directed Energy (SCADE) mission. JDEC accelerates research, prototyping, integration, testing, manufacturing readiness, and fielding of high-energy laser and high-power microwave capabilities. NSTXL serves as consortium manager.
organizations.label: Joint Directed Energy Consortium (JDEC)
organizations.rawParent: Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies (ASW(CT))

organizations.description: The AEDC Velocity Alliance is an Air Force Test Center and Arnold Engineering Development Complex consortium-based initiative established under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 to accelerate modernization of national test infrastructure for next-generation defense systems. The Government manages the consortium directly and uses the alliance as a pre-qualified industrial base for rapid competition of complex engineering, construction, and test-infrastructure modernization projects.
organizations.label: AEDC Velocity Alliance

organizations.description: Army Contracting Command–Redstone Arsenal is a major contracting center subordinate to U.S. Army Contracting Command. ACC-RSA provides contracting, acquisition, and business advisory support for aviation and missile systems, research and development, prototyping, limited production, and other Army missions, and administers the Department of War Drone OTA Consortium.
organizations.label: Army Contracting Command–Redstone Arsenal (ACC-RSA)

organizations.description: The Department of War Drone Other Transaction Authority Consortium is a government-managed 10 U.S.C. § 4022 vehicle administered through Army Contracting Command–Redstone Arsenal. It provides a standing pathway for rapid prototyping and follow-on production of drone and related warfighter solutions for Department components and other authorized users. A Government Steering Committee governs consortium membership, solicitations, evaluations, and awards; there is no external consortium manager.
organizations.label: Department of War Drone OTA Consortium
